F-22 fidelity implementation guide

Implementation plan: The system-by-system overhaul plan lists the changes, priorities and dependencies. Detailed findings and evidence remain in this audit.

Purpose: Compare the mod’s behavior with documented F-22 behavior, use named aircraft analogues where F-22 details are unknown, and provide a durable guide for implementation. This is a full re-audit of the previous report.

Revision baselines: Initial full review 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT; deeper gap analysis 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT; evidence challenges 2026-10-27 04:44:12 MDT. 223 behavior comparisons. All 115 original comparisons and all 343 supporting records have review dispositions. Captures contain 556, 565 and 565 text files respectively. These are per-file reads of shared, actively edited source. Each case identifies its capture; aircraft implementation and binaries were not changed by this audit.

Assessment and meaning of the results

The mod already represents several narrow documented behaviors and many useful aircraft-system abstractions. It also has specific documented F-22 omissions, identifiable differences from selected substitutes, and important areas whose numerical fidelity cannot be determined from public evidence. There is no defensible whole-aircraft accuracy percentage. The reference-specific comparison and its evidence boundary are the result.

This revision corrects earlier overclaims. It credits narrow matches, separates genuine differences from deliberate interface choices, and does not treat an unknown F-22 schedule as an error. A working system is not automatically authentic; a different internal implementation can reproduce the documented outward behavior accurately.

Verification means source/reference review. Exact cited code locations were checked against captured file hashes. Complete cited passages were read where access allowed; indexed-only/403 sources are identified in the reference ledger. Proposed acceptance cases have not been flown in DCS. No undisclosed radar, engine, flight-control or defensive-system performance is certified.

Evidence and applicability

  1. Use dated F-22 operator, USAF, manufacturer or primary-authored engineering evidence for the particular behavior it establishes. A rescue document establishes emergency equipment functions, not a production performance deck or complete pilot procedure.
  2. Where F-22 behavior is unknown, name the Viper/Hornet analogue and make an explicit adoption decision. Their different control rules are alternatives; they are not a combined mandatory F-22 specification.
  3. General radar/AESA and flight-physics sources constrain plausible simulation behavior. General crew-alerting guidance supplies optional design ideas. Civil certification guidance is not an F-22 operating rule. Agreement with a principle does not authenticate production coefficients, operating timing or APG-77/F119 curves.
  4. Keep unsupported details unresolved or bounded as estimates. A modernization requirement, demonstration or development-era design is not proof of fleet-wide current installation.

Chuck’s guides and ED manuals/tutorials describe DCS aircraft. The legacy Hornet guide describes its APG-73 radar; public APG-79 material supplies separate AESA context. F-22 references span 1999–2000 development flight tests, 2001 architecture, 2006 rescue equipment, dated operational rules and later manufacturer/USAF accounts. WP00 resolves the intended aircraft configuration before dependent fixes.

Reference tier Comparisons Interpretation
F22 documented 60 Dated F-22-specific function/behavior; scope and equipment applicability still apply.
F16/Hornet analogue 124 Named substitute or comparison, not proof of an F-22 error.
General flight-physics evidence 20 Physical relationships and public capability anchors, not authenticated F-22 curves.
General radar/AESA evidence 13 Public general radar principles and observable game approximation.
General crew-alerting evidence 6 Optional general cockpit-design comparator; civil guidance does not establish military aircraft requirements.
Closeness label Meaning
Matches documented behavior The narrow stated benchmark agrees. Unknown values or other parts of the system remain outside that match.
Partly matches A stated portion agrees and a concrete remaining difference is identified.
Contradicts documented behavior The stated implementation conflicts with evidence in its stated tier. Check the tier: a physics conflict is not a recovered F-22 manual limit.
Missing documented behavior The cited function/principle has no corresponding behavior in the inspected owned paths; declared era/equipment and host limits still apply.
Diverges from selected analogue Difference from the named alternative or general substitute. Adoption remains explicit.
Not assessable from available evidence No defensible closeness conclusion for this particular property. This is not a failure grade.

Confidence describes the stated comparison, not the likelihood that the entire aircraft is accurate. The counts are scope bookkeeping, not a weighted fidelity score.

How to use this guide for the project

Start with WP00, then work through the dependency order below. Open the relevant finding, retain its evidence boundary, and implement the proposed observable behavior. Every case includes normal operation, limits and failure/recovery acceptance. Positive matches are retention criteria; unknowns are evidence/calibration tasks; optional analogue differences require a recorded design choice.

Use a finding ID in each implementation change. Record the chosen baseline/substitute, new source revision, affected dependencies and acceptance evidence. Close only the stated behavior. “Implemented,” “tested” and “F-22 documented” are separate facts. This document proposes changes; it does not mark them completed.

Priority Meaning
P0 Resolve configuration/evidence/dependency decisions before dependent implementation.
P1 First implementation tranche: documented functional omissions or a concrete user-path/physical inconsistency.
P2 Follow-on depth and coherent normal/limit/degraded behavior.
P3 Optional/interface/analogue policy choice; not automatically a required F-22 fix.

WP00 · Freeze the aircraft and evidence baseline

Dependencies: None; baseline decision first.

Choose a dated F-22 configuration and equipment list. Record each supported real behavior, adopted analogue and unresolved parameter before writing fixes. Preserve explicit alternatives when sources conflict.

Completion evidence: A configuration sheet identifies era/software/equipment, land-based recovery, optional equipment exclusions and adopted substitutes. No modern requirement is silently treated as fleet-wide fielding.

Scope: AV31, AN26, AN30, AS27, AX01, AX09, AX10, AX13, AX14.

WP01 · Correct the physical model and define performance envelopes

Dependencies: WP00

Resolve the CG/force-point dependency, identify any host ground-effect contribution and add the missing owned contribution where needed; then calibrate thrust, drag, fuel and approach behavior under matched conditions. Keep public capability anchors separate from unknown production curves.

Completion evidence: An envelope matrix records mass, CG, stores/doors, pressure altitude, temperature, wind and engine setting for steady climb/cruise, acceleration, turn, approach and ground-roll cases. Source-limited parameters remain estimates with stated bounds.

Scope: PF01, PF02, PF03, PF04, PF05, PF06, PF07, PF08, PF09, PF10, PF11, PF12, PF13, PF14, PF15, PF16, PF17, PF18, PF19, PF20, PF21, PF22, AV01, AV13, AV19, AV35, VG01, VG02, VG03, VG04, VG05, VG06, VG07, VG08, VG09, VG10, VG11, VG12.

WP02 · Make power, starting, hydraulics and emergency sources coherent

Dependencies: WP00

Define consumer supply and surviving-source topology; add the documented SES/APU/emergency gear functions, then resource recovery, compartment isolation and hook function. Do not copy Hornet start/gear hardware over known F-22 evidence.

Completion evidence: Normal, single-source-loss, dual-source-loss and exhausted-reserve scenarios have consistent achieved consumer states. Restoration never creates energy or replays a stale command.

Scope: AV02, AV03, AV04, AV05, AV06, AV07, AV15, AV16, AV17, AV26, AV31, AV32, AV33, AX03, P11.

WP03 · Connect fuel, oxygen, cabin and cooling dependencies

Dependencies: WP01, WP02

Separate stored fuel from feed availability, preserve finite start/APU combustion accounting, and connect engine bleed, cabin/OBOGS and supported backup. Define thermal/fault indications only within available references.

Completion evidence: Stored-versus-feed quantity, mass debit and warning state agree through depletion, supply loss and recovery. Estimated rates/thresholds are not presented as F-22 operating limits.

Scope: AV08, AV10, AV11, AV12, AV20, AV21, AV22, AV23, AV30, AV34, AV36, AV37, P17, VT01, VT02, VT03, VT04, VT05.

WP04 · Build a coherent navigation and approach instrument chain

Dependencies: WP00, WP02

Provide independent navigation-source/reversion behavior, valid LOC/GS/TACAN components, coherent barometric/radar altitude and defined landing-cue geometry. Calibrate the E-bracket against the aerodynamic model rather than transplanting another aircraft AoA.

Completion evidence: A land-based recovery matrix covers manual visual/ILS/TACAN/overhead where adopted, missed approach/go-around, component loss, touchdown, braking and refueling-state indications. CASE I/II/III and carrier ACLS remain comparator procedures unless deliberately added as optional equipment.

Scope: AN01, AN02, AN03, AN04, AN05, AN06, AN07, AN08, AN09, AN10, AN11, AN12, AN13, AN27, AN28, AN29, AV09, AV24, AV25, AX18, AX19, AX16, NG01, NG02, NG03, NG04, NG05, NG06, NG07, NG08, NG09, NG10, NT01, NT02.

WP05 · Resolve AFCS engagement, override and recovery interactions

Dependencies: WP01, WP04

Use one explicit AFCS substitute interaction policy, decide and label ordinary-paddle versus dedicated-override behavior per mode, and correct altitude/heading request paths. Then complete guidance, degraded disengagement and ATC if adopted. Separate advisory terrain escape from any supported automatic recovery.

Completion evidence: Pilot selection, engagement gates, axis ownership, temporary override, permanent disconnect, recapture and power/fault recovery agree in both cockpit and flight response. Optional autoland/automatic collision recovery requires a separately justified baseline.

Scope: AN14, AN15, AN16, AN17, AN18, AN19, AN20, AN21, AN22, AN23, AN24, AN25, AN26, AN30, AV27, AV28, AV29, P19, P20, P21.

WP06 · Give radar tasking observable AESA depth

Dependencies: WP00, WP02

Define an observable game task-service model with explicit coverage, track priority, revisit/age, saturation and reduced-array states. Align focus and native sensing; keep rendering, detection and estimate updates separate.

Completion evidence: Controlled task-load/coverage cases show the declared service tradeoffs. Silence stops new own-radar measurements; powered passive receivers and donor sources continue and age their own observations. No invented APG-77 range, waveform, LPI invisibility or scheduler is claimed.

Scope: AS01, AS02, AS03, AS04, AS05, AS06, AS07, AS08, AS09, AS10, AS11, AS12, AS13, AS14, AS15, AS16, AS17, AS18, AE01, AE02, AE03, AE04, AE05, AE06, AE07, AE08, AE09, AE10, AE11, AE12, AE13, AE14, AE15, AE16, AE17, AX11.

WP07 · Preserve evidence through identification, fusion and networks

Dependencies: WP06

Keep observation time, receipt time, donor/source, identity conflict and pilot declaration distinct. Build independent freshness for each source/field and, if adopted, planned-intelligence behavior before expanding display convenience.

Completion evidence: Conflicting, late, duplicate, stale and lost-source observations never become unwarranted hostile certainty or a fresh own-sensor measurement.

Scope: AS10, AS11, AS12, AS19, AS20, AS25, AS26, AS27, AX02, AX17, ST01.

WP08 · Complete warning and countermeasure program semantics

Dependencies: WP00, WP02

Manual program work can proceed independently; WP07 is a dependency only for later threat-input integration into SEMI/AUTO. Adopt the existing flat Hornet-like scheme coherently, or explicitly choose a nested alternative. Separate edit/display bank from execution bank; add declared draft/save, mode/consent, interruption, inventory and readiness rules.

Completion evidence: Generic inert timing/inventory scenarios establish selection/execution, bounds, partial exhaustion, power interruption and restore without any threat-specific recipes, effectiveness assumptions or automatic defensive optimization.

Scope: AS21, AS22, AS23, AS24, CP01, CP02, CP03, CP04, CP05, CP06, CP07, CP08, CP09, CP10, CP11.

Dependencies: WP01, WP04, WP06, WP07

Separate sensor cue, actual seeker acquisition, readiness, mission initialization, programming, release conditions, actual release and inventory. Keep training and jettison distinct.

Completion evidence: A declared supported-store set has normal, rejected, stale, inhibited, power-loss and acknowledgement cases with achieved status. Unsupported TGP/HMD/HARM/Maverick/naval weapons are equipment decisions, not automatic F-22 defects.

Scope: AS28, AS29, AS30, AS31, AS32, AS33, AS34, AS35, P22, P23, P24, P25, P26, P27, P28, SG01, SG02, SG03, SG04, SG05, SG06, SG07, SG08, SG09, SG10, SG11, SG12.

Integrate the owned radio workflow, truthful achieved readback and surviving CNI functions. Retain coherent display layouts, held-command release and brightness/fault separation; add optional map/checklist/planned-intelligence depth only under the adopted policy.

Completion evidence: Tuning, receive/audio, focused controls, numeric commit/cancel, display relocation, lighting and surviving CNI all follow their stated contracts across failures and restoration.

Scope: AX01, AX02, AX03, AX04, AX05, AX06, AX07, AX08, AX09, AX10, AX11, AX12, AX13, AX14, AX15, AX16, AX17, AX18, AX19, C01, C02, C03, C04, C05, C06, C07, C08, CG01, CG02, CG03, CG04, CG05, CG06, CG07, CG08, CG09, CG10.

WP12 · Validate integrated alert lifecycle and coupled failure recovery

Dependencies: WP02, WP03

Give each supported equipment condition its own validity, occurrence and acknowledgement state. Keep terrain/navigation gates, audio suppression, master attention and downstream utility supply states distinct. Optional general cockpit-design ideas remain adoption choices.

Completion evidence: Fault A acknowledged plus new fault B re-alerts as adopted; independent faults survive unrelated sensor loss; clearing a detected temperature does not falsely restore an isolated supply. Synthetic probes and runtime observations retain separate evidence scopes.

Scope: CG01, CG02, CG03, CG04, CG05, CG06, CG07, CG08, CG09, CG10.

WP11 · Close findings with evidence and keep the guide current

Dependencies: WP01, WP02, WP03, WP04, WP05, WP06, WP07, WP08, WP09, WP10, WP12

Implement in bounded changes tied to finding IDs. Attach the new code revision, normal/limit/degraded observations and reference version to each closure; update dependencies and assumptions when a correction changes the target.

Completion evidence: Closure requires evidence for the stated behavior, not merely a passing callback/test or a matching label. A fully tested estimate remains an estimate; new primary evidence can reopen it.

Finding Corrected interpretation
AV04 The Eaton normal-System-2/maintenance-transfer statement does not provide the entire hydraulic schematic. The previous categorical crossfeed contradiction was too strong.
AV15, AV21, AV26, AV31 The 2006 USAF rescue document supplies direct F-22 evidence for SES starting, separate fuel feed/transfer, pneumatic emergency gear and a 28 V battery domain. Do not present the Hornet rotate/pull-handle, accumulator/free-fall sequence as documented F-22 behavior or call the low-voltage battery supply wrong.
AV24 The Viper guide conflicts on the exact parking-brake release RPM. Only release with power advance is retained as the comparator target.
AN02 The AFMAN positive-position procedure does not mandate a manual INS-filter correction UI. TACAN/GPS awareness can satisfy part of that task; deeper manual fixes are an explicit substitute choice.
AN16 Dedicated override bindings implement temporary release/recapture; the ordinary HOTAS paddle routes to permanent autopilot-off. The former broad match was incorrect.
AS21 / CP02 CHAF/FLAR/RPT/INT is substantially Hornet-like. Independent Viper BQ/BI/SQ/SI hierarchy is a different alternative, not proof the flat scheme is inherently insufficient.
AS09 Reviewed WACQ elevation descriptions conflict by edition. Do not turn a disputed number into a required F-22 geometry.
R15 Configured compensation limits do not describe actual stabilization; the native flags are disabled after body reprojection. Judge the complete path.
SC28 / AS35 The published F-22 SMS emergency-jettison role is direct evidence, not merely an analogue feature.
AS25 / D03 Datalink receipt age differs from observation age; DEF/TSD coast policies also need consistency.
AX01 A published display-role description does not specify the power-up layout or exact active aperture.
AX02 The narrow integrated multi-source picture is credited as a match; undisclosed real fusion precision alone is not a documented shortfall.
AX13 Hornet second CLR clears option windows. The cited passage does not establish equipment deselection or page navigation.
AX18 / AX19 Unmapped draw arguments do not prove absent refueling transfer; Boolean light exports prove lost owned dimming, not a measured real-world luminosity error.

Executed analysis probes

The actual captured warning Lua policy was executed in Lua5.1 with synthetic states. It produced a first caution, no new event after acknowledgement while the combined caution stayed true, and a new event after full clear/reassert. Ground or navigation-invalid inputs returned blank policy output; independent native/discrete indications were not exercised. The probe supports those state-path observations only. Comparator-specific voice inhibits and production F-22 behavior remain unresolved. Full inputs/scope/results are retained in the verification companion.

This pass adds 8 further comparisons and 21 targeted reviews, anchored to 2026-10-27 04:44:12 MDT. It tests premises as well as implementation paths. Control-path reproduction scope

Actual captured Lua owners were executed with synthetic parameters and native stubs. The heading probe supplied the checked degree-valued publication contract: 0° acknowledged, while1°,90°,123° and359° applied by that simulated publisher falsely timed out. A dropped NAV receiver left achieved latitude unchanged while a same-ID edit reported ENTERED. The same recognized focused radar format moved its horizontal cursor at primary focus2 and stayed still at3/4/5 in both A/A and A/G, with a healthy synthetic A/G backend. These reproduce the specified state paths; they do not establish native DCS integration, renderer behavior or flight response. Other probes retain their individual scope/results in the verification ledger.

Uncertainty and calibration register

These are explicit project decisions or evidence gaps. Do not fill them by copying arbitrary comparator numbers and then present the result as documented F-22 behavior. A source-limited estimate can be coherent and useful while remaining an estimate.

Property What is known / unresolved Next decision or evidence
Aircraft configuration Historical architecture and emergency equipment are documented; current software/equipment fit is not established by every source. WP00 selects era/equipment and optional functions; preserve dated applicability.
Approach AoA/E-bracket The mod uses12 degrees; the continuation found a historical F-22 EMD12-degree on-speed anchor and11.5-degree single-engine test-law change. Production applicability and exact bracket/indexer widths remain unknown. Reconcile the selected-era reference with lift, weight, trim, configuration and cue geometry; do not treat another aircraft’s AoA as the F-22 calibration. AN04, PF16, VG05
Thrust, drag, fuel and high-alpha envelope Public broad capability anchors exist; installed full-condition performance and production curves are unknown. Use matched-condition sweeps and physically consistent bounded estimates; do not claim validated turn/climb/departure limits. PF02, PF13, PF19

AV01 · Integrated pitch-only thrust vectoring and physical travel

Basis: F22 documented · Matches documented behavior · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT.

F-22 evidence boundary: Pratt & Whitney documents this capability directly.

Reference behavior: F119 nozzles vector up/down as much as 20 degrees; nozzle management is integrated with F-22 flight controls and regulated by FADEC. F-22 / F119 · Exceptional Combat Performance / Delivers Unparalleled Aircraft Maneuverability.

Our captured behavior: A common pitch-derived command drives left/right achieved nozzle states, bounded to ±20 degrees; each nozzle produces a rotated thrust vector. Mach/WOW scheduling reduces available travel.

Closeness and exact difference: The narrow documented pitch-axis, maximum-travel and integrated-command behavior matches. The proprietary Mach/gear schedule and reversion behavior remain unknown; they do not lower this narrow match.

Implementation target: Retain integrated pitch vectoring with an absolute ±20-degree mechanical bound. Label the mod’s Mach, gear and hydraulic schedules as estimates rather than asserting that the brochure authenticates them.

Applicability / unresolved details: Production engine capability; no claim that ±20 degrees is available at every flight condition.

Proposed acceptance — normal: At a supported low-Mach condition, compare command, achieved left/right angle and force direction.

Proposed acceptance — limits: Sweep each mechanical bound and the estimated Mach/gear schedules.

Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Remove one hydraulic supply; retain independent achieved nozzle states and opposite-engine behavior.

Dependencies: TVC command, Per-side hydraulic state, Physical forces and animation.

Re-audit: Confirmed. Narrow manufacturer pitch-axis/travel/integration claim remains supported; proprietary schedules are explicitly outside the match.

Captured implementation: EFM/source/VehicleSystems.h:36, EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:703, EFM/source/RAPTOR.cpp:1018.

Proposed acceptance — limits: Keep limited consumer capacity and conditioning requirements explicit; one ready indication does not certify all outputs.

Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Stop/fault APU, then restore a qualified source; all dependent physical supplies and indications follow the declared handoff.

AV03 · Four pressure-compensated engine-driven pumps

Basis: F22 documented · Not assessable from available evidence · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT.

F-22 evidence boundary: Supplier component brochure documents the pump architecture.

Reference behavior: Four engine-driven variable-displacement pumps are rated 72 gpm each with 4,100 psi pressure compensation. F/A-22 / F-22 · 7.

Our captured behavior: Two spool-driven pressure states target 3,950 psi; pressure rise/decay is fixed-rate and no individual pump or demand flow exists.

Closeness and exact difference: Two pressure states could abstract four physical pumps in normal operation. The code does not expose enough flow/demand behavior to compare the published pump capability under load. A 4,100-psi pump rating is not proof that every cockpit/consumer indication must read 4,100.

Implementation target: Represent four pumps feeding the intended circuits sufficiently to preserve single-pump redundancy and reduced available flow. Keep pump outlet rating, regulated pressure and displayed consumer pressure distinct; do not declare 3,950 wrong without identifying its measurement point.

Applicability / unresolved details: Supplier hardware specification, April 2014; total flow ratings do not establish simultaneous full flow at all conditions.

Proposed acceptance — normal: Document pump-to-circuit abstraction and steady pressure/flow at one and two engines.

Proposed acceptance — limits: Exercise concurrent demand against reduced source capacity without assuming the sum of rated flows is always available.

Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Compare individual pump loss with full circuit loss and recovery.

Dependencies: Circuit map, Pump availability, Demand representation, Pressure measurement definition.

Re-audit: Qualified. Confirmed four pump specification, but two pressure states can abstract four pumps. Outlet compensation is distinguished from cockpit/consumer pressure.

Captured implementation: EFM/source/VehicleSystems.h:13, EFM/source/VehicleSystems.h:88.

AV04 · Utility normal supply is distinguished from maintenance transfer

Basis: F22 documented · Not assessable from available evidence · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT.

F-22 evidence boundary: Supplier describes a specific utility switching function.

Reference behavior: Utilities normally supplied by System 2 can receive System 1 pressure through a maintenance switching valve. F/A-22 / F-22 · 6.

Our captured behavior: Gear, flaps, generic speed brake and most controls use actuator_available derived from max(left,right) pressure at all times, without a maintenance crossfeed selection.

Closeness and exact difference: The owned model has no explicit normal-System-2 versus maintenance-System-1 utility transfer distinction. Eaton establishes that switching function but is not a complete schematic excluding every automatic backup path, and the mod left/right states have not been mapped to real System 1/2. The prior categorical claim of unrestricted feed contradicting the entire real utility system was too broad.

Implementation target: Identify the actual utility consumers and mapping before changing failed-side behavior. Represent the documented normal/maintenance transfer distinction where applicable. Preserve independent flight-control redundancy; do not use this brochure alone to forbid every automatic backup path.

Applicability / unresolved details: Documented maintenance switching function only; not a complete circuit schematic or authenticated left/right mapping.

Proposed acceptance — normal: Identify the actual consumers controlled by the documented utility selector and their normal source.

Proposed acceptance — limits: Compare maintenance transfer with ordinary operation after circuit mapping is established.

Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Lose a normal source and check only documented or explicitly estimated backup behavior.

Dependencies: Consumer mapping, Maintenance selection, Independent flight-control feeds.

Re-audit: Corrected. Withdrew the categorical whole-system contradiction. Eaton does not establish every backup path or the mod left/right mapping; the missing explicit transfer distinction is narrower.

AV05 · Rudder retains supply from either hydraulic system

Basis: F22 documented · Matches documented behavior · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT.

F-22 evidence boundary: Supplier identifies automatic rudder supply selection.

Reference behavior: A differential-pressure-operated rudder shuttle selects between two independent hydraulic systems. F/A-22 / F-22 · 2.

Our captured behavior: Rudder actuator availability uses the greater remaining normalized left/right hydraulic supply, so a healthy opposite side can keep the rudder moving.

Closeness and exact difference: The narrow documented surviving-supply function matches: the healthy independent side remains available to the rudder. The source supplies no switching transient that would justify penalizing the mod’s instantaneous max-supply abstraction.

Implementation target: Retain the functional ability to power the rudder from either independent side, preserving physical supply isolation and any documented switching delay if later found. Do not require detailed valve geometry merely to count the hardware.

Applicability / unresolved details: Functional comparison of the documented shuttle; no authenticated transient data.

Proposed acceptance — normal: Command rudder with both hydraulic supplies healthy.

Proposed acceptance — limits: Limit one supply while retaining the other; compare achieved rudder motion.

Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Fail either side independently, then both; restore one side without healing physical damage.

Dependencies: Rudder actuator, Independent supplies.

Re-audit: Confirmed. Either surviving hydraulic source can retain modeled rudder authority, consistent with the documented shuttle function; no unpublished switching transient is demanded.

Cockpit/Scripts/Systems/EW_Programs.lua:15, Cockpit/Scripts/Systems/Combat_Logic.lua:116, Cockpit/Scripts/Systems/MFD_Controls.lua:100.

F-22 evidence boundary: F-22 programmable dispensing is documented, but editable field sets, count and cockpit edit choreography are not.

Reference behavior: Hornet programming exposes CHAF, FLAR, RPT and INT and an explicit SAVE action; STEP selects the manual program. Viper separately uses independent chaff/flare BQ/BI/SQ/SI fields and standby editing. These are alternative schemas, not cumulative F-22 requirements. The Viper guide also distinguishes ordinary selected programs from dedicated direct-access programs; it does not justify equating every direct-access program with physical BYP mode. DCS F-16CM Block 50 · pp 586-592 controls, mode and individual field definitions, DCS F/A-18C Lot 20 · pp 610-612 ARM, CHAF/FLAR/RPT/INT, SAVE and STEP.

Our captured behavior: Three programs have independent chaff/flare counts, one shared interval and total-event repetitions, substantially resembling the flat Hornet four-field schema. Powered bezel edits immediately alter the selected editable bank. CMS-up/left/push execute fixed banks 1/2/3, so the displayed/editable selection is not the normal-dispense selector.

Closeness and exact difference: Programmable manual dispensing and the flat field structure are already present. Actual differences are immediate editing without SAVE, fixed execution-bank mapping instead of normal selected-program execution, and no defined standby/edit mode. Independent nested Viper timing is an optional alternate model, not proof that the Hornet-like structure is inaccurate.

Implementation target: Adopt the simpler Hornet-like generic game schema as the initial baseline: clearly define total cycles, selected normal-dispense bank, direct-access bank, draft/SAVE editing and edit permissions. Preserve three banks as an explicit mod estimate. Offer independent per-type BQ/BI/SQ/SI only as an optional deeper model, without real tactical presets.

Adoption decision: selected analogue. Flat Hornet-like generic programs are selected; nested Viper timing is optional, not additive mandatory scope.

Applicability / unresolved details: Selected analogue is a design benchmark; the F-22 procedure is not established by those aircraft manuals.

Proposed acceptance — normal: Edit a draft then SAVE; normal dispense uses selected bank.

Proposed acceptance — limits: Empty/bounded fields and total-events label have explicit meaning.

Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Cancel/power loss before SAVE preserves last committed program.

Dependencies: CP02, CP03, CP04.

AS03 · Search return becoming an established TWS track

Basis: F16/Hornet analogue · Partly matches · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 03:35:59 MDT.

F-22 evidence boundary: Published F-22 documents do not give track-initiation thresholds.

Reference behavior: Viper distinguishes search, track, system and bugged targets. It normally establishes a track after detections on two consecutive sweeps; a search return is not immediately equivalent to a mature track. DCS F-16CM Block 50 · pp 189-190.

Our captured behavior: Quality becomes mature when cumulative hits>=2 and age is within freshness. Hits increment on a new observation timestamp and are not explicitly reset after a missed sweep.

Closeness and exact difference: The guide says two consecutive sweeps is the usual condition, not an unconditional universal law. The mod counts new observation timestamps cumulatively and cannot identify an eligible missed revisit from that counter alone.

Implementation target: Adopt distinct tentative/mature/coasting track behavior. A consecutive-revisit promotion rule is a proposed Viper analogue, not an authenticated F-22 threshold; record eligibility before treating a missed revisit as evidence of loss.

Requirement basis: Proposed analogue; adoption requires an explicit mod design decision

Applicability / unresolved details: Selected analogue is a design benchmark; the F-22 procedure is not established by those aircraft manuals.

Proposed acceptance — normal: Repeated genuine detections promote a tentative file.

Proposed acceptance — limits: A missed eligible revisit between hits prevents a claimed consecutive-hit promotion.

Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Reacquisition is distinguished from a never-interrupted track.

Dependencies: AE05, Observation and revisit identity.

Re-audit: Qualified. Re-read says usually two consecutive sweeps; changed a categorical threshold into a selected analogue and distinguished timestamps from actual sweep eligibility.

VG01 · Fuel/store redistribution changes angular inertia as well as mass and CG

Basis: General flight-physics evidence · Not assessable from available evidence · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

F-22 evidence boundary: F-22 fuel capacity/external tanks are public; exact tank geometry and production inertia tensors are not.

Reference behavior: Rotational inertia depends on mass distribution and squared distance from each axis. Equal total mass and CG need not imply equal response to the same torque. General flight/utility physics · 17, F-22 · Internal/external fuel capacity.

Our captured behavior: Burn/refill transactions carry position and mass, but every queued moment-of-inertia change is zero. Current inertia is received from the host. The included API says DCS performs internal mass/CG/inertia calculations, so zero local MOI does not prove the host keeps inertia fixed.

Closeness and exact difference: The open issue is the complete host-plus-EFM angular response after redistribution, distinct from the already identified moving wing force point. The host may infer point-mass inertia from the supplied location; that contract must be established before adding another correction.

Implementation target: Establish which inertia contributions DCS derives from position/mass and which the EFM must supply, then preserve mass, first moment and angular inertia consistently. Use estimated lumped tank/store geometry; do not invent a measured F-22 tensor.

Applicability / unresolved details: Generic rigid-body relation; host contract and production numbers unresolved.

Proposed acceptance — normal: Compare equal-mass/equal-CG cases with different spanwise fuel/store distribution and the same small applied moment.

Proposed acceptance — limits: Compare partial/full tanks and a mirrored asymmetric installation without assuming current inertia has changed merely because mass changed.

Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Remove/refill a station and verify host and EFM each account for the change exactly once.

Dependencies: DCS mass/inertia contract, Tank/store geometry abstraction, Host current inertia.

Re-audit: New case. Prior UV15/PF07 covered mass transactions and force moment arms; this isolates rotational inertia and angular acceleration.

VG02 · Air-relative force is invariant to a uniform ground/wind translation

Basis: General flight-physics evidence · Matches documented behavior · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:17:52 MDT.

F-22 evidence boundary: No F-22-specific coefficient is required for the reference-frame relationship.

Reference behavior: At fixed achieved configuration in free air, aerodynamic force depends on aircraft velocity relative to air. Adding the same uniform velocity to aircraft and air leaves that aerodynamic condition unchanged. Tire/ground behavior instead depends on motion relative to the runway. General flight/utility physics · Ground reference / wind speed / airspeed / wind tunnel equivalence, General flight/utility physics · Nomenclature: true and ground speed.

Our captured behavior: World velocity minus world wind supplies aerodynamic speed/Mach/q. The body-state callback independently subtracts body wind for drag direction. Horizontal world velocity supplies ground-speed steering/brake gates. These are the correct narrow frame distinctions; consistency of the two host callback vectors has not been flown.

Closeness and exact difference: Both relevant relative velocities are represented instead of treating groundspeed as aerodynamic speed. A host callback orientation/sign mismatch is still possible and is not ruled out by reading the subtraction alone.

Implementation target: Retain the frame distinction. Verify airborne aerodynamic-force invariance at fixed achieved configuration with ground-interaction gates inactive and matching body/world vectors. Separately preserve wind-dependent takeoff/landing groundspeed, automatic ground schedules and wheel motion.

Applicability / unresolved details: Narrow airborne mathematical/frame match at fixed achieved configuration; no numerical F-22 force validation or invariance requirement for changed ground interactions.

Proposed acceptance — normal: Airborne, hold achieved configuration, air-relative velocity/AoA/density and all other force inputs fixed, with ground-interaction gates inactive. Translate world aircraft and wind velocity equally and provide matching body vectors; aerodynamic outputs should agree.

Proposed acceptance — limits: In the isolated airborne case, compare crosswind/tailwind and near-zero airspeed/groundspeed without changing achieved configuration.; Evaluate ground roll separately: with the runway fixed, changed groundspeed may legitimately alter automatic flap targets, braking, steering and wheel forces. Do not require those outputs to be invariant.

Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Provide inconsistent or invalid body/world inputs as diagnostic cases, not as claims that real wind changes aircraft coefficients.

Dependencies: Host body/world coordinate contract, Wind callbacks, Ground contact.

Re-audit: New case. PF20 addressed atmospheric sensitivity; this isolates wind invariance and ground-relative versus air-relative consumers.

Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Inject invalid sensor data separately from real load and verify it does not become a valid limiter demand.

Our captured behavior: Five causes are ORed into one caution boolean. caution_ack remains true as long as that boolean stays true. Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Source invalidity, power loss and mission reset do not revive old acknowledgements or erase a genuine new occurrence.

Basis: General flight-physics evidence · Matches documented behavior · Confidence: moderate · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:44:12 MDT.

F-22 evidence boundary: The reviewed public F-22 material does not disclose automatic cold-temperature compensation or its pressure-altimeter implementation.

Reference behavior: FAA describes indicated/true altitude divergence in nonstandard temperature and distinguishes pressure-setting changes from temperature correction. Its civil procedure explicitly does not accomplish cold correction by changing QNH. Viper/Hornet pressure-altimeter descriptions confirm that pressure setting and altitude indication are distinct quantities; none establishes a F-22 automatic compensation feature. General atmospheric/instrument behavior · Complete effect-of-temperature and setting-versus-correction paragraphs; section 5(a), DCS F/A-18C benchmark · p 54 pressure-source/setting description, DCS F-16C benchmark · p 54 servo-pneumatic altimeter description.

Our captured behavior: NativeAltimetry uses EFM static pressure and an ISA pressure-height relation with selected pressure datum. It does not replace indicated altitude with geometric ASL or change the conversion to the current ambient temperature. This preserves a pressure-based indication when the host atmosphere supplies nonstandard pressure/height relationships. The actual host weather-column behavior has not been exercised here.

Closeness and exact difference: This is a narrow quantity/model distinction: finite/fresh barometric data can be healthy while differing from geometric altitude. The magnitude of weather error, position error and any actual F-22 compensation remain outside the match.

Implementation target: Retain indicated pressure altitude as a separate quantity from geometric altitude and any optional temperature-corrected guidance. Do not mark normal weather-related disagreement invalid or silently change QNH to force agreement; any compensation feature needs its own declared state and evidence.

Do not mark normal weather-related disagreement invalid or silently change QNH to force agreement; any compensation feature needs its own declared state and evidence.

Proposed acceptance — normal: For a declared nonstandard atmosphere, compare pressure-derived indication and true geometry without forcing equality.

Proposed acceptance — limits: A healthy nonstandard-temperature indication remains distinguishable from stale/nonfinite pressure; resetting QNH is not a generic temperature-correction command.

Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Actual pressure/source failure triggers its validity policy without erasing the separately available geometric clearance used by other systems.

Dependencies: Host atmosphere characterization, Pressure datum, Altitude validity/source matrix.

NT02 · Healthy barometric altitude is coupled to unrelated CAS computation in the HUD

Basis: F16/Hornet analogue · Not assessable from available evidence · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:44:12 MDT.

F-22 evidence boundary: A particular F-22 ADC/HUD partial-failure blanking rule is not disclosed by the reviewed public sources.

Reference behavior: Hornet p 54 and Viper p 54 describe pressure-altitude paths with their own input/reversion behavior. FAA distinguishes pitot-only airspeed errors from static-source errors affecting multiple instruments. This supports a chosen component-specific validity model; it does not prove that every real integrated HUD must retain altitude after every ADC fault. DCS F/A-18C benchmark · p 54 standby altitude/airspeed dependencies, DCS F-16C benchmark · p 54 altimeter source/reversion, General pitot/static instrument principles · Complete 8-10/8-11 blockage-of-pitot/static discussion.

Our captured behavior: HUD_Flight_Data resets HUD_ALT_VALID and only sets it inside a successful CAS-conversion branch, despite separately valid F22_ALT_BARO_VALID/F22_ALT_BARO_FT. Executed captured Lua with healthy baro, velocity and bridge state but invalid TAS produces upstream baro-valid 1/FPM-valid 1/HUD-alt-valid 0. Restoring TAS restores altitude. Conversely, invalid baro alone leaves CAS displayed. UFD/MFD baro counters use the independent upstream validity.

Closeness and exact difference: A fresh source labelled healthy by the mod is hidden because a different quantity cannot be calculated. This is a demonstrated synthetic source-state dependency. The cited standalone-instrument principles do not establish the exact integrated Hornet/F-22 HUD blanking policy, so it is not graded as a proven real-aircraft contradiction.

Implementation target: Under the selected component-specific validity policy, gate/update pressure altitude independently of CAS conversion. A common ADC/static failure can still invalidate several outputs through explicit shared-source health; do not encode that failure indirectly as every unsuccessful CAS calculation.

Adoption decision: declared physics/component-dependency model. Under the selected component-specific validity policy, gate/update pressure altitude independently of CAS conversion. A common ADC/static failure can still invalidate several outputs through explicit shared-source health; do not encode that failure indirectly as every unsuccessful CAS calculation.

Applicability / unresolved details: Selected generic/analogue partial-data behavior. Actual physical failure generation, integrated-ADC failover and Raptor display policy require separate evidence.

Proposed acceptance — normal: With fresh baro and valid flight-path data, invalidate only the TAS/CAS input and retain the chosen healthy baro display.

Proposed acceptance — limits: When a declared common static/ADC failure invalidates both source families, inhibit both explicitly; keep independent UFD/HUD source semantics consistent.

Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Restore the individual input and recover only its affected presentation without stale-value jumps or spurious source changes.

Dependencies: Air-data component-health policy, HUD_Flight_Data, NativeAltimetry/Altitude_System.

ST01 · Ownship identification replies are a separate function from interrogating other contacts F22 documented Missing documented behavior · P1

ST01 · Ownship identification replies are a separate function from interrogating other contacts

Basis: F22 documented · Missing documented behavior · Confidence: high · Priority: P1 · Code capture: 2026-10-27 04:44:12 MDT.

F-22 evidence boundary: The dated F-22 CNI description explicitly includes MK XII interrogation and transponder functions. Detailed current modes, keys, cockpit pages and operational reply policy are not established by this chapter.

Reference behavior: A modeled ownship transponder answers valid incoming interrogations according to its own state; requesting SCAN/LOS identification of another contact is a separate operation. Viper and official Hornet references make that distinction visible through transponder state and interrogation settings. Their exact controls and cryptographic procedures are not adopted as F-22 facts. F-22 design as published 2001 · PDF pp 8-9, section 32.3.3, DCS F-16CM Block 50 · pp 639-642, DCS F/A-18C · pp 62-63, IFF Panel, DCS F/A-18C Lot 20 · p 638 and pp 642-645.

Our captured behavior: The owned IFF page offers AUTO, SCAN IFF and LOS IFF. Radar_IFF controls acceptance of contact classifications and publishes the common interrogator enable from radar/main power. No independent ownship transponder operating state, reply indication or pilot emergency-identification state was found in the captured CNI/device/input paths. Any automatic simulator identity response is therefore unverified host behavior, not evidence that these owned interrogation controls implement the transponder role.

Closeness and exact difference: The current workflow covers asking about other aircraft; it does not establish the separately documented F-22 function of answering identification requests. A radar contact marked friendly, own PPLI transmission and a transponder reply must not be treated as interchangeable evidence. The absence finding applies to the owned simulation workflow; it does not assert that the DCS host never identifies the aircraft automatically.

Implementation target: Add a declared abstract ownship-identification state and a visible distinction between transponder available/replying/unavailable and interrogator requests. Use supported host capabilities or clearly labeled game events, with a documented emergency-identification option if retained. Do not implement real cryptography, real waveforms or claim recovered F-22 menu choreography; do not disable a surviving transponder merely because the radar is off unless the selected simulated supply/resource state requires it.

Applicability / unresolved details: The ownship identification role is a dated direct F-22 requirement. Exact modes, codes, timing and UI are proposed substitutes. DCS Viper itself does not fully implement code editing, so its guide is not proof of complete cryptographic fidelity.

Proposed acceptance — normal: With transponder enabled, a qualified incoming game interrogation yields the declared reply/indication; SCAN/LOS actions still query other contacts independently.; Radar off with surviving CNI power preserves the independently supported responder role under the adopted supply policy.

Proposed acceptance — limits: Absent or incompatible abstract identification credentials do not produce an authenticated friendly reply. No real encryption or protocol is modeled.; Own PPLI availability alone is not shown as proof that a separate transponder replied.

Proposed acceptance — failure and recovery: Loss/recovery of CNI supply or the selected resource fault shows unavailable/recovered identification state without silently inheriting interrogation consent.; Emergency identification, if offered, has an explicit pilot-selected state and clear reset behavior.

Dependencies: AX03 CNI recovery, AS10-AS12 identity provenance, Declared equipment baseline, Qualified host incoming-interrogation support.

Re-audit: New case. Distinct missing role established by the dated F-22 chapter and checked against both named DCS aircraft. Full capture searched for transponder/mode/IDENT control owners; no such owned path was found.

Cockpit/Scripts/MFD_COMMON/adi_page.lua:21
P19 · Numeric transaction isolation
corrected		 The active UFC uses drafts/pending readback. Stores now waits for ENTRY_FIELD zero before acknowledgement: credit that change. HEADING still applies math.deg to a degree-valued EFM parameter, and same-ID waypoint acknowledgement remains a separate weaker transaction. Separate these from the chosen physical commit key.
Continuation: Repeated physical UFC mouse input now has release messages in the captured transport. That is credited separately from the still-present heading-unit and same-waypoint-ID acknowledgement issues. Executing the actual UFC controller with a simulated publisher matching the checked EFM degree contract applied requests at 0°,1°,90°,123° and 359°. Zero acknowledged; the other four tested values falsely timed out as NO RESPONSE. This confirms a valid-target/readback mismatch for those cases; it does not show the real aircraft flew the requested heading or prove every nonzero value fails. The missing-receiver waypoint probe separately reports ENTERED with requested latitude 42 and achieved latitude 41.5 for the unchanged displayed waypoint ID.
Related: AX12, N10

confirmed		 Coarse 100m LOS samples can miss a narrow terrain crossing between samples; subsequent bisection only refines a crossing already detected. A synthetic ridge is a valid numerical acceptance case; this is not measured operational F-22 accuracy.

confirmed		 Waypoint designation captures coordinates on the command edge and acknowledges a sequence, guarding against one-tick display lag. Keep this positive handoff separate from the UFC existing-point same-ID acknowledgement.

qualified		 Power loss clears the owned target; selected waypoint-source targets can persist through mode changes. Separate stored mission coordinates from a fresh sensor track/release consent; the exact F-22 memory policy remains unknown.

qualified		 Waypoint-to-ground-target handoff derives terrain elevation. Planned flight altitude is a different quantity and should not automatically become impact elevation. Building/roof offsets and source uncertainty remain explicit limitations.
Related: Bounded engineering/inventory observation.
Cockpit/Scripts/Systems/AG_Mark_System.lua:187

qualified		 AAR request and external argument 22 are separate channels; cockpit indication uses another argument. Map actual meanings before grading contact/disconnect fidelity. No conclusion that host fuel transfer is absent follows.

Fourteen earlier cached English tutorial transcripts remain preserved in the source collection (thirteen ED/Wags and one ancillary landing tutorial). Their metadata and URLs remain reference aids; main conclusions use the cited passage appropriate to each case. A separate terrain-avoidance video had metadata only because its transcript was inaccessible. Full transcripts are not republished in this guide.

Consolidated source library and retired-report provenance

At the user's instruction, this master replaces the earlier separate audit/review reports. 27 report files are removed and the previous audit index is replaced in place. Implementation handoffs, test plans and research-source documents are retained as supporting material.

The accompanying complete source catalogue preserves the original 1,362 extracted reference entries from 95 documentation files and the earlier research pass, with subsequent agent-reviewed references appended. These are reference entries, not a count of independently authenticated research publications. The catalogue carries web URLs, repository references, local/internal paths, original labels and citation locations. Reference sections from the retired reports are preserved as well, including bibliographic context not reducible to a URL.

Imported material retains its historical provenance and is not silently promoted into current implementation or flight evidence. Some resources may be old, unavailable, duplicated across editions or comparison-only. Private ABI/disassembly notes describe DCS implementation contracts, not real F-22 specifications. Code references pinned to old commits remain historical.

The web-resource index below is included directly in this audit for browsing. The JSON catalogue also carries every repository/code and local/internal reference with its citing documents and line numbers.

Audit package and completion boundary

This is the single master audit. HTML and Markdown present the same guide, synchronized to the shared mod’s docs/audit/README.md. The 27 superseded audit reports remain removed; their 28 report/provenance entries and all imported source references remain preserved. Supporting JSON files are companion data, not competing audit reports.

Use the behavior comparisons, verification ledger, implementation plan, supporting register, coverage map and source catalogue when carrying findings into code changes. The source-drift companion records later live changes relative to this pinned capture; it does not silently update this revision’s conclusions. The captured text-source ZIP preserves reproducibility without relying on later live line numbers.

Every prior recorded claim has a disposition, but public evidence does not permit exhaustive verification of the actual F-22. Hidden production schedules, full aircraft envelopes, current fleet fit, EDM argument meanings and host-native behavior remain limited where stated. Those limits are explicit work items and decisions, not assumed inaccuracies. No new aircraft code, binaries, installed runtime or DCS flight was changed or operated by this re-audit.

Reference-specific closeness, proposed implementation and runtime qualification are separate. Dated source captures and review updates are identified in the guide.
